# Lustro

> A browser-based, agent-friendly debugging library for Android. Lustro embeds a small web server in an app's debug builds and serves its tools as tabs that a desktop browser opens over adb. The built-in Network tab captures OkHttp traffic, shows the messages of OkHttp WebSockets, and can mock responses, throttle connections, and replay requests. Every tab is also a JSON API under `/api/v1/`, so agents and scripts can use it directly.

Facts to get right when you add Lustro to an app:

- Coordinates: `io.github.twinsen81:lustro:0.1.0-SNAPSHOT` is the debug runtime, and `io.github.twinsen81:lustro-noop:0.1.0-SNAPSHOT` is a no-op with the same API for release builds. Add `lustro` with `debugImplementation` and `lustro-noop` with `releaseImplementation`. They declare the same Gradle capability, so they cannot be on one configuration.
- A `-SNAPSHOT` version resolves only from the Sonatype Central snapshots repository, `https://central.sonatype.com/repository/maven-snapshots/`.
- Lustro needs `minSdk` 24, `compileSdk` 35, Android Gradle Plugin 8.6, and Kotlin 2.0. It does not raise the app's own dependency versions: OkHttp 4.12.0 or newer (5.x included) and `androidx.lifecycle` 2.4.1 or newer stay as they are, and Lustro has no coroutines dependency.
- Build Lustro once, in `Application.onCreate()`, and call `start()` there, on the main thread. Add every tab with the builder, before `build()`: after `start()`, `addTab()` throws.
- Add `lustro.networkInterceptor()` with `addInterceptor`, not `addNetworkInterceptor`, after the app's own interceptors that change the URL, the headers, or the body.
- The interceptor shows only the handshake of a WebSocket. To capture the messages, create the sockets with `lustro.webSocketFactory(okHttpClient).newWebSocket(request, listener)`, or pass that `WebSocket.Factory` to the library that creates them. `lustro-noop` returns the client itself.
- To send requests from the console through the app's clients, pass `senders = listOf(OkHttpSender.create("API", baseUrl = "https://api.example.com") { apiClient })` to `NetworkDebugTab.create`. Lustro calls the lambda only at the first send, so the client can be the one built with `lustro.networkInterceptor()`, and the requests sent from the console are captured.
- For an HTTP client that is neither OkHttp nor platform `HttpURLConnection`, report each request to `lustro.networkCaptureSink()`: `beginRequest`, then `completeRequest` or `failRequest`. `lustro-noop` returns a sink that records nothing.
- The Logs plugin serves the app's own logcat under `/api/v1/logs/`: add `io.github.twinsen81:lustro-logs:0.1.0-SNAPSHOT` with `debugImplementation` and `io.github.twinsen81:lustro-logs-noop:0.1.0-SNAPSHOT` with `releaseImplementation`, and register `LogsDebugTab.create()` with the builder. It needs no data source and no permission. Its log lines are not redacted.
- The Preferences plugin reads and edits the app's SharedPreferences and Preferences DataStores under `/api/v1/prefs/`: add `io.github.twinsen81:lustro-prefs:0.1.0-SNAPSHOT` with `debugImplementation` and `io.github.twinsen81:lustro-prefs-noop:0.1.0-SNAPSHOT` with `releaseImplementation`, and register `PrefsDebugTab.create(context, files = listOf(PrefsFile("settings", prefs, ValuePolicy.VISIBLE)))`. A file's `ValuePolicy` is `VISIBLE`, `MASK_SENSITIVE` (the default), or `KEYS_ONLY`; `readOnly = true` makes edits answer `403`. Register a Preferences DataStore with `dataStores = listOf(PrefsDataStore("app_state", dataStore))`; the tab writes through the app's own instance. The other files in `shared_prefs` and `files/datastore` are discovered, masked, and read-only; a discovered DataStore is always read-only. Pass `store=preferences_datastore` to pick a DataStore in a route.
- The SQLite plugin reads the app's SQLite and Room databases under `/api/v1/sqlite/`: add `io.github.twinsen81:lustro-sqlite:0.1.0-SNAPSHOT` with `debugImplementation` and `io.github.twinsen81:lustro-sqlite-noop:0.1.0-SNAPSHOT` with `releaseImplementation`, and register `SqliteDebugTab.create(databases = listOf(SqliteDb.support("app") { roomDb.openHelper.writableDatabase }))`. `SqliteDb.framework` takes a framework `SQLiteDatabase`, and `SqliteDb.file(name, file)` a file that the tab opens read-only for each request. `discoverFrom = context` also lists the other database files in `databases`. The GET routes browse: `GET databases`, `tables?db=`, `schema?db=&table=`, and `rows?db=&table=`, a page in `{ items, nextCursor }` with `limit`, `filter`, `sort`, and `dir`. `POST query` with `{ db, sql }` runs a statement on a connection that SQLite opens read-only, for every database. `POST exec` (`{ db, sql }`), `POST edit` (`{ db, table, rowid | key, values }`), and `POST delete` write, only to a database registered with `writable = true`, and answer 403 for any other. `query` and `exec` refuse BEGIN, SAVEPOINT, and the other transaction statements, ATTACH, DETACH, and VACUUM, and `exec` every PRAGMA.
- The WorkManager plugin shows the app's WorkManager work and the events of each run under `/api/v1/work/`, and needs WorkManager 2.12.0 or newer: add `io.github.twinsen81:lustro-work:0.1.0-SNAPSHOT` with `debugImplementation` and `io.github.twinsen81:lustro-work-noop:0.1.0-SNAPSHOT` with `releaseImplementation`, register `WorkDebugTab.create(context, uniqueNames = listOf("sync"))`, and pass the app's `Configuration.Builder` through `tab.configure(builder)` from a variant-split bootstrap, with on-demand initialization (`Configuration.Provider`, and `WorkManagerInitializer` removed from the manifest). `configure()` forwards every event to the listeners that the app set before. `GET items` polls the work in the cursor envelope, `GET items/{id}` gives one with its events, `GET events` polls the events (enqueued, started, finished with `result` and `output`, stopped with `stopReason`, exception with the stack trace) in the stream envelope, `GET metrics` reads work-analytics when the app passes its `WorkMetricsInfoRepository` as `metrics`, `POST cancel` takes `{ id }`, `{ name }`, or `{ tag }`, and `POST prune` deletes finished work. `state.listeners` in each response says whether there are events, and `state.reason` why not. The events live on the heap and end with the process.
- Custom tabs are `DebugTab` subclasses, and they must be in `src/debug`. The published lint check `LustroDebugUsageInRelease` reports them in other source sets.
- The server binds `127.0.0.1:8080` on the device, and listens only while the app is in the foreground. Reach it with `adb forward tcp:8080 tcp:8080`.
- Every API request needs the token from the `LustroToken` logcat line (`Lustro ready endpoint=http://127.0.0.1:8080 token=<token>`), sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A device that drops Info logs drops that line; a debuggable app also keeps the token, host, and port in `adb shell run-as <package> cat shared_prefs/lustro_debug.xml`. `GET /api/v1/_meta` lists the tabs, and `GET /api/v1/<id>/_schema` returns a tab's OpenAPI document.

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Twinsen81/Lustro/main/README.md): install, quick start, capture options, mock rules, the security model, custom tabs, and troubleshooting
- [Driving Lustro from agents](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Twinsen81/Lustro/main/docs/AGENTS.md): token discovery, authentication, the wire protocol, and the Network, Logs, Preferences, SQLite, and WorkManager routes, for agents that use a running Lustro
- [Security policy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Twinsen81/Lustro/main/SECURITY.md): the threat model, and what keeps Lustro out of release builds

## API contracts

- [Network tab OpenAPI document](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Twinsen81/Lustro/main/lustro/src/main/assets/lustro/network.openapi.json): the contract of the `/api/v1/network` routes
- [Logs tab OpenAPI document](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Twinsen81/Lustro/main/lustro-logs/src/main/assets/lustro/logs.openapi.json): the contract of the `/api/v1/logs` routes
- [Preferences tab OpenAPI document](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Twinsen81/Lustro/main/lustro-prefs/src/main/assets/lustro/prefs.openapi.json): the contract of the `/api/v1/prefs` routes
- [SQLite tab OpenAPI document](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Twinsen81/Lustro/main/lustro-sqlite/src/main/assets/lustro/sqlite.openapi.json): the contract of the `/api/v1/sqlite` routes
- [WorkManager tab OpenAPI document](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Twinsen81/Lustro/main/lustro-work/src/main/assets/lustro/work.openapi.json): the contract of the `/api/v1/work` routes
- [Wire protocol v1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Twinsen81/Lustro/main/wire-protocol/v1/README.md): the shared envelopes, their JSON Schemas, and the versioning policy

## Tools

- [lustro CLI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Twinsen81/Lustro/main/lustro-cli/README.md): a Python command-line client for the HTTP API. `lustro open` forwards the port and opens the console with the token
- Agents: use the `lustro` CLI rather than curl, and keep its output small with `lustro net list --errors --last 20`, `lustro net get <id> --no-body`, and `lustro net body <id> | head -c 4000`. `lustro net wait --url <text> -- <command>` runs the command and waits for the request it causes, and `lustro net export --har out.har [--ids <id> ...]` saves transactions as a HAR file. For WebSockets, `lustro net ws list` prints the connections, `lustro net ws events <id> --last 20` the last events of one, and `lustro net ws payload <id> <seq>` one message's payload. `lustro api GET <tabId>/<route> --param key=value` (or `POST ... --body '<json>'`) sends a request to any route, also of a tab without commands of its own, and prints the response: `lustro api GET logs/text --param level=W` prints the app's warnings and errors, `lustro api GET prefs/entries --param file=<name>` a SharedPreferences file, `lustro api GET sqlite/rows --param db=<name> --param table=<table>` a page of a table's rows, and `lustro api GET work/events --param type=finished,exception` the results and failures of the app's workers
